findings.where: scheduler.py:4096-4097 (unchanged) reached through the new deferral in schedule_policy.py add_chunked_req
findings.issue: When the continuation is parked (0 < budget < grid, remainder does not fit) and the same round still admits another request (ax_protect keeps scanning for short hits, scheduler.py:4062-4072; a request needing fewer than `budget` new tokens fits), can_run_list is non-empty, so get_new_batch_prefill runs `self.chunked_req.inflight_middle_chunks += 1` although the parked request is not in the batch. No result ever decrements that phantom count.
findings.consequence: At the request's real final chunk the counter is still 1, so batch_result_processor takes the middle-chunk branch (lines 315/375): prefill_finished_time is not set, the first output token is not appended and the request is merged into decode without it. Expect a wrong/shifted output or a stall and a broken TTFT record (prefill_finished_time 0) for every affected request.
findings.why_new: The existing parks (106 at budget <= 0, hybrid-SWA) leave no room for another admission, so can_run_list is empty and the function returns at line 4077 before the increment.
findings.fix: Count and pass the continuation only when it is actually scheduled: e.g. `in_batch = self.chunked_req is not None and self.chunked_req in can_run_set`; increment inflight_middle_chunks only if in_batch; pass chunked_req=(self.chunked_req if in_batch else None) to ScheduleBatch.init_new; chunk_deduct 0 when not in_batch. Alternative: stop admitting others in a parked round (costs short-hit latency).

findings.issue: In a parked round extend_range is the previous chunk, so #pending-token is deducted by a chunk that did not run. Log-based chunk inference (pending deltas) must exclude parked rounds; the guard from finding 1 fixes it.

No deadlock found: grid = lcm(page, truncation_align, mamba checkpoint grid) is a multiple of 64; cap is rounded up to >= grid (scheduler.py:1347-1349); the continuation is added first so rem_input_tokens is full; the park ends once rem_total_tokens >= grid, which finishing decodes provide. Starvation is possible if admitted short hits keep consuming the freed trickle; the trace's deferred_decisions/elapsed_s will show it. Theoretical corner: a prompt within one grid of the whole pool with an empty running batch would park indefinitely (before: crawled on).
findings.action: Watch deferred_decisions/elapsed_s in 072; no change required.

findings.issue: Parked continuation keeps extend_range.end == len(prefix_indices), so the next round skips the stash (scheduler.py:3674), matching the existing parked-chunk contract; init_next_round_input re-runs without side effects for a continuation; no mamba ping-pong or track state is touched while parked.

Only the ax_protect continuation path changes; protection off keeps native unaligned progress (as documented). New-request truncation is already page-aligned (schedule_policy.py ~1575-1592) and grid is a multiple of 64, so in this configuration non-final misaligned prefixes come only from the sub-grid continuation this patch parks. Final chunks are unaffected by design.

The park decision depends only on allocator/budget state, identical across TP ranks, as before. Trace hooks never influence scheduling; rank-0-only request attributes (_ax_alignment_*) are read only for logging. _rank_zero() needs the TP group, available in scheduler processes, and is only called when enabled.

ax_chunk_alignment imports only stdlib at module level (parallel_state lazily), no import cycle; ENABLED is read at import, so the env must be set at launch (it is inherited by scheduler processes). 2 MiB lifetime budget per TP0 process with explicit exhaustion; fields are Python ints/bools; hooks are O(1) per extend request. Moving cand_extend_input_len earlier does not change its value.
